$comment: The curated allowlist: which public SJSU pages the knowledge base is built
from. `python -m kb.ingest --sync-seeds` upserts these into public.kb_sources
on `url`.
Every URL here returned HTTP 200 with content-type text/html when probed on
2026-09-30. That matters more than it sounds: plausible-looking paths like
/faso/how-to-apply/, /bursar/tuition-and-fees/, /scholarships/,
/parking/visitors/, /tours/ and /maps/ are all 404, and /housing/ is a
redirect loop. A seed list written from memory would be a third dead links.
Two entries are the redirect *target*, not the path you would guess:
/facultyaffairs/ -> /up/        (University Personnel)
/ecampus/        -> /cfeti/     (and /ecampus/ is Disallow'd in robots.txt)
crawl_depth is 0 everywhere. SJSU's advertised sitemap (indexmap.txt) is a
2013-2016 artifact whose per-department sitemaps all 404, so there is no
cheap discovery mechanism -- and for a corpus this size a human picks better
pages than a breadth-first crawl does. The column exists for later.
audience_tags is a relevance boost, never an access filter: a page tagged
`student` is still the right answer to a guest asking about it. Access is
`visibility`, which is enforced in RLS and in the retrieval functions.
fetch_interval_minutes: 10080 is weekly. catalog.sjsu.edu gets 43200
(monthly) because its robots.txt sets crawl-delay: 120 -- about 30 pages an
hour -- so it is an overnight job and must not share a run with the rest.
--- 2026-10-01: six URLs added after a coverage pass ------------------------
Mapped the KB-eligible questions in bench/questions.jsonl onto this list and
found half of them had no page here. Two things that pass came out of it:
* Of the 16 faq/long bench questions, only **10 can reach retrieval at
all**. Four are conversational ('thanks!', 'Can you make that shorter?')
and are caught by prepare_rag_query's gates; two are time-sensitive and
are refused by services/freshness.py by design. The plan's '16/16'
coverage target was unreachable by construction, not by seed gap.
* **student-faq-2 ('What GPA do I need to stay in good academic
standing?') has no page on this list and no obvious public landing page
to add.** Ten candidate paths 404, and reading the actual links out of
/registrar/, /advising/ and /ue/ surfaced only grade-change and
grade-forgiveness pages. The policy lives in the catalog or in a Senate
S-policy, both of which need crawl_depth > 0 or the slow catalog host.
So expect 9 of 10, not 10 of 10, and do not read the miss as a
retrieval failure.
Already covered, verified by fetching rather than assuming: /visit/ carries
campus-tour content (13.7k chars, mentions tours) for guest-faq-2, and
/parking/ mentions VTA (7.1k chars) for guest-long-2 -- thin for 'which
lines stop closest', but it is the only page SJSU publishes for it.
`enabled: false`, kept in the file rather than deleted, because the URL is
right and only the crawl depth is wrong.
At crawl_depth 0 the catalog gives one page, and that page is pure navigation:
16 chunks of 'Catalog Home / Colleges and Departments / Academic Programs /
Policies and Procedures / ...' with no policy text behind it. Measured against
the 10 KB-eligible bench questions, it was top-1 for exactly one --
student-faq-2, 'What GPA do I need to stay in good academic standing?' -- which
it answers WRONGLY: the retrieved text contains no '2.0', no 'GPA', no 'good
standing' and no 'probation'. It ranks because a nav list is full of words like
'Academic' and 'Requirements'. It appeared in no other question's citations.
So its only measurable effect on the bench set was to turn a known coverage gap
into a confident wrong answer, which is worse than no answer. The catalog is
still the highest-value source in the corpus -- course descriptions, degree
requirements, the academic standing policy itself -- but it needs
crawl_depth > 0, and at crawl-delay 120 that is its own overnight job.
